newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian banks to cut rates from April 1.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian banks to cut rates from April 1.

text.p: Slovenian banks will reduce interest rates on deposits by about 1.5 percent from April 1, the Office for Protection of Competition said on Wednesday.

"The accord of the Slovenian Bank Association, which we approved this week, is the third in a row of similar pacts and will be valid for a year," Andrej Plahutnik, director of the Office for Protection of Competition, told Reuters.
Lending interest rates were expected to follow the movement in deposit interest rates, he added.
Average interest rates for tolar deposits of between 31 and 90 days were at 4.9 percent in January, up from 4.8 percent in the same month of 1996.
Interest rates on short-term capital loans fell to 11.3 percent from 12.1 percent in January of the previous year. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
